title: George Lewis, Chicago migration and railroad passes
summary: They discuss where musicians have gone, and Williams explains how railroad passes let him travel but limited him on some routes.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: George Lewis is still alive, eh?
No, George Lewis goes all over the world.
He goes to Germany and California. Goes to Russell Woods.
I don't believe he's never coming back here anymore.
Armstrong? No, I don't think the play, he might come in to see his family.

He been away for a good while, too. I believe he left here before Ed Atkin left. Went to Chicago. A lot of guys went to Chicago. But all the towns I traveled, I liked New York better than I grew. Any of them towns I've been in. I liked New York.
But I guess working for the railroad, you could travel, huh? Well, I got a little handicapped.

I used to go anywhere in the United States. But now, in some railroad, I have to be half back. I had to pass the railroad. I had to pass to go to Seattle, Washington. It cost me $40.00. That's half back for me. I'm on my own basketball in Seattle. So I said I ain't going. I got a daughter in Portland, and that would be about $20.00. Well, she just went here, but a year ago, and her brother died. So I wait later. If I have to pay her to go see her.
